title: agentic-sdlc finding
description: One finding, from any agent or any deterministic tool, in the shape every stage can compare. A finding is a claim about the code; this schema is what makes the claim checkable by something other than the agent that made it. Valid JSON is not proof of correct reasoning — the gate still independently checks the evidence.

id.description: Stable identity for this finding, assigned by `sdlc finding write`. Referenced by the commit that closes it.

category.description: Taxonomy address. A letter domain plus a check number (`D.31` = Security / injection), or a cross-cutting domain (`X7` = agent economics). Domains are listed in docs/control-spec.md.

ruleId.description: The rule in docs/control-spec.md this finding was raised under, e.g. SEC-INJECTION-SQL. Stable across versions; a renamed rule is a new rule.

component.description: The module, package or service the finding belongs to. Free text, but consistent within a repository.

summary.description: One sentence stating the defect. Not the fix, not the consequence — the defect.

evidence.description: What makes this a finding rather than an opinion. A finding with no evidence is itself a finding against the agent that raised it.

code.description: The relevant lines, quoted — not paraphrased.

toolOutput.description: The deterministic output that supports the claim: compiler diagnostic, analyser line, failing assertion, scanner hit. Null for an llm-detected finding, which is why such findings carry lower confidence by default.

repro.description: The smallest sequence that reproduces it, as commands. The brief's rule: a finding you cannot reproduce may simply be wrong.

classification.description: Severity and confidence are deliberately separate axes. A low-confidence fix for a critical vulnerability is not safe merely because the agent believes it solved the problem.

severity.description: How bad it is if real. critical: auth bypass, data corruption, exploitable injection. high: memory-safety, race, broken authorization, destructive migration. medium: performance regression, missing edge case, incorrect retry. low: formatting, lint, safe mechanical refactor. advisory: a trade-off or a disputed judgement — report, never force.

confidence.description: How sure we are it is real. high: a deterministic tool said so, or there is a reproduction. medium: strong reading of the code, no execution. low: pattern match or suspicion. Never raise confidence to justify an automatic repair.

exploitability.description: Security findings only. Describe reachability; never write an exploit.

impact.description: What goes wrong for a user or an operator if this is not fixed.

rootCause.description: Why the problem exists, not the visible symptom. A finding with only a symptom tends to produce a symptom-only fix, which is the failure X4 exists to prevent.

change.description: The minimal change. Not a refactor of the surrounding module.

expectedBehaviour.description: What is true after the change that is not true now.

sideEffects.description: What else this touches, including anything downstream.

autofixEligible.description: Whether the repair policy in docs/control-spec.md permits an agent to make this change unattended. Derived from severity and confidence together; never from severity alone.

verificationPlan.description: The specific test, static check, benchmark or experiment that would establish the repair worked. Written before the repair, so the repair cannot choose its own easy standard.

outcome.description: open: raised, not yet addressed. fixed: behaviour changed and a test proves it. refused: the finding is wrong, with the evidence. deferred: real, out of scope, filed where it will be seen. unexecuted: the fix could not be verified — not closed. escalated: awaiting a human decision. These extend the remediator's existing four; the five evidence words (passed/failed/skipped/refused/unexecuted) describe a criterion, not a finding.

closedBy.description: The commit that closed this finding. One finding per commit, so this is a single sha.

provenance.description: Who claimed this, with what, and against what state. Without it a finding cannot be reproduced or disputed.

agent.description: The agent or tool that raised it, e.g. sdlc-security-reviewer, gitleaks.

model.description: The model behind an llm-detected finding, where the host exposes it.

detection.description: How it was found. The brief's rule 2: prefer a tool to an opinion, and record which this was so a reader can weigh it.

commit.description: The commit the finding was raised against. A later commit does not void a finding the way it voids a receipt, but it does mean the line numbers may have moved.
